title: Continuatio Fragmentorum ex Adversariis mathematicis depromptorum

deep.reconstruction: Setting q = π/4, Euler writes the odd-denominator sums so that odd powers alternate in sign and even powers do not: Σ_{k≥0} (−1)^k/(2k+1)^n for n odd (Dirichlet β(n)), and Σ 1/(2k+1)^n for n even (λ(n) = (1−2^{−n})ζ(n)). He sets each sum equal to 2^{n−1} a_n q^n, with a_1 = A, a_2 = B, a_3 = C, and so on. The coefficients satisfy a_1 = a_2 = 1 and a_n = (Σ_{i+j=n} a_i a_j)/(2(n−1)). This is the coefficient form of the Riccati equation y' = (1+y²)/2 for y(x) = Σ a_{n+1} x^n. Its solution with y(0) = 1 is y = sec x + tan x, so a_n = A_{n−1}/(n−1)!, where A_m are the Euler zigzag (up/down) numbers 1, 1, 1, 2, 5, 16, 61, 272, 1385, 7936, 50521, 353792. In modern form, β(odd) and λ(even) together equal (1/2)(π/2)^n · A_{n−1}/(n−1)!. Euler tabulates a_1 through a_12 in factored form: 277/8064, 62/2835, 50521/3628800 and 1382/155925 are a_9 to a_12. All values check. Dividing the even-index coefficients B, D, F, H, … by 2(2^{2m}−1) = 2·3, 2·15, 2·63, 2·255 gives ζ(2m)/π^{2m} = 1/6, 1/90, 1/945, 1/9450. This undoes the factor (1−2^{−2m}). Second part: with χ the nontrivial character mod 4, he recalls two Euler products from the previous page. The first is π/4 · Π_{p≥3} (p−χ(p))/p = 1, which is L(1,χ)^{−1}. The second is π/2 · Π (p+χ(p))/p = 1, from Π(1+χ(p)/p)^{−1} = L(2,χ0)/L(1,χ) = (π²/8)/(π/4). Dividing one by the other removes π: the factor 1/2 cancels against the p = 3 factor 2, leaving Π_{p≥5} (p−χ(p))/(p+χ(p)) = 1. Taking logarithms and expanding log((1+1/p)/(1−1/p)) = 2Σ_{k odd} 1/(k p^k) gives Σ_{k odd} (1/k) Σ_{p≥5} χ(p)/p^k = 0; this expansion is completed on the next page. Purpose: express the slowly convergent prime series S = 1/3 − 1/5 + 1/7 + 1/11 − … = −Σ_p χ(p)/p as 1/3 + Σ_{k≥3 odd} (1/k) Σ_{p≥5} χ(p)/p^k. This series converges rapidly and shows S is slightly larger than 1/3; the true value is about 0.33498.
errors: In the quotient product, the factor printed '20/22' should be 20/18. It is the p = 19 factor, where χ(19) = −1, so (19+1)/(19−1) = 20/18; 20/22 is not a factor of the prime-wise quotient at all, since the p = 23 factor is 24/22. It is either a slip in the manuscript or a misprint in the 1862 edition.
The products are only conditionally convergent: they are taken over primes in increasing order, and Euler's term-by-term manipulations of logarithms are formal. The results are nevertheless correct.
Not on this page, but downstream: the Corollary on the next page restates S with the wrong sign pattern (+1/11 should be listed with the 4n−1 primes as +, i.e. 1/3 − 1/5 + 1/7 + 1/11 − 1/13 …).

ideas.what: Unified closed form for β(2m+1) and λ(2m) as 2^{n−1} a_n (π/4)^n, with the a_n determined by a quadratic convolution recurrence (equivalently, Taylor coefficients of sec x + tan x)
ideas.modern_name: Euler/zigzag numbers; generating function sec + tan for alternating permutations; Dirichlet beta at odd integers and λ at even integers
ideas.usually_credited_to: Euler for the sums (1730s–1740s); the zigzag/alternating-permutation interpretation to D. André (1879); the unified form is often re-presented, e.g. Elkies (2003)
ideas.where_published: Euler's papers on reciprocal power sums (e.g. E61, 'De summis serierum reciprocarum… dissertatio altera', 1743) and Introductio in analysin infinitorum (E101) Vol. I ch. X; Euler numbers also in Institutiones calculi differentialis (E212). Exact presence of this recurrence there: unsure.

ideas.what: Recovering ζ(2m)/π^{2m} (1/6, 1/90, 1/945, 1/9450) from the even coefficients via the divisors 2(2^{2m}−1)
Prime products for π/4 and π/2 over odd primes, with p ± χ(p) as neighbouring even numbers
ideas.modern_name: Euler products for L(1,χ4) and for L(2,χ0)/L(1,χ4)

ideas.what: Dividing the two products to eliminate π, then taking logs to express Σχ(p)/p through Σχ(p)/p^k for odd k ≥ 3, giving a fast-converging series for the prime series S
ideas.modern_name: Acceleration of prime L-series sums: log L(s,χ) and Möbius-type expressions for prime zeta/L sums (Σ_p χ(p)/p^s = Σ μ(m)/m · log L(ms, χ^m))
ideas.usually_credited_to: Euler for this series; modern systematic forms to Glaisher, Landau and later work on prime zeta functions
ideas.where_published: E596 'De summa seriei ex numeris primis formatae 1/3 − 1/5 + 1/7 + 1/11 − 1/13 − …' (Opuscula analytica II, 1785), where Euler evaluates S ≈ 0.3349816

deep.surprise_reason: Everything here is a notebook version of material Euler himself published. The β/λ coefficients appear in E61 and the Introductio, the prime products in E72, and the prime-series transformation in E596. The only small point of note is the explicit Riccati-type convolution recurrence tabulated as far as the zigzag numbers 50521 and 353792 in factored form, which is well understood today.
transcription_corrections: The quotient product reads '1·4/6·8/6·12/10·12/14·16/18·20/22·etc.' in the image, so the transcription is faithful; mathematically the last factor should be 20/18.
In L q^{11} the denominator is '256·81·25·7' (a product; 256·81·25·7 = 3628800 = 10!); the missing multiplication dot in the transcription '256 81.25.7' could mislead.
